scenes.title: THIS WEEK'S SHOOTING STARS ARE COMET DUST
scenes.say: Those shooting stars this week? That's dust from Halley's Comet, hitting us at sixty six kilometers a second.

scenes.title: Faster than a bullet. Way faster
scenes.say: A jet does nine hundred an hour. A rifle bullet, about three thousand. This dust? Over two hundred thousand.

scenes.title: It burns up before it lands
scenes.label: GONE BEFORE THE GROUND
scenes.say: At that speed it crushes the air in front of it until it glows. Over a hundred kilometers up, the grain is already gone.

right.title: THE STREAK
right.sub: a glowing trail in the sky
right.verdict: you can see it from the ground

scenes.say: The twist: the dust is tiny, like crumbs of ash. Almost all the glow is superheated air.

scenes.label: HALLEY'S COMET'S NEXT VISIT. ITS LAP TAKES ABOUT 76 YEARS
scenes.src: Star Walk / NASA: Halley's period ~76 years, perihelion 28 July 2061
scenes.say: The comet itself won't be back until twenty sixty one. Its dust shows up every October.

scenes.title: SEEN ONE YET?
scenes.say: Seen one yet? Comment yes, not yet, or clouds.
